subject: Child pedestrian struck near elementary school
summary: A Waymo vehicle struck a child near a Santa Monica elementary school during drop-off hours. NHTSA is examining its speed, precautions around children, and response after the collision.

subject: Passing stopped school buses
summary: A Waymo vehicle reportedly passed a stopped school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. NHTSA is investigating whether its automated driving system responds safely and legally to stopped buses.

subject: Tesla Cybercab federal safety certification audit
summary: NHTSA opened an audit query into Tesla's certification of the Cybercab, which lacks conventional steering, braking, and accelerator controls. Investigators are examining the technical basis for Tesla's claim that the vehicle complies with federal motor vehicle safety standards, including whether Tesla considered certain standards inapplicable.

subject: Traffic-safety violations with FSD engaged
product: Tesla vehicles equipped with FSD (Supervised) or FSD (Beta)
summary: NHTSA is investigating reports of Tesla Full Self-Driving driving through red lights, entering oncoming traffic lanes, and taking incorrect lanes at intersections.

subject: FSD collisions in reduced roadway visibility
summary: NHTSA is examining Tesla Full Self-Driving crashes in fog, glare, or other poor-visibility conditions. The investigation focuses on whether the system recognizes reduced visibility and gives drivers enough warning.

subject: Unexpected ADS behavior
summary: NHTSA reviewed reports of Waymo vehicles striking stationary objects, entering opposing lanes, and driving into construction areas. The concern is whether the automated driving system reliably handles unexpected road conditions.

subject: Unexpected ADS braking
summary: Two Zoox vehicles were rear-ended after unexpectedly braking near other road users. NHTSA investigated whether the automated driving system could trigger unnecessary hard braking.

subject: Purpose-built vehicle certification
summary: NHTSA examined whether Zoox properly certified its purpose-built driverless vehicle against federal safety standards. The audit closed after Zoox obtained a demonstration exemption for the vehicles.

subject: ADS behavior around pedestrians
summary: NHTSA examined Cruise vehicles' behavior near pedestrians, including whether they yielded and exercised appropriate caution. The case closed after a related recall and Cruise's suspension of public-road driverless operations.

subject: Hard braking and immobilizations
summary: NHTSA investigated reports of Cruise vehicles braking sharply or becoming immobilized in traffic. The case closed following a software recall intended to reduce unexpected braking.

subject: Autopilot driver engagement and misuse
summary: NHTSA investigated whether Tesla Autopilot adequately monitored driver attention and prevented foreseeable misuse. The analysis closed following a recall intended to strengthen driver-engagement safeguards.
